page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-100s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, designed with a focus on memory allocation relative to compute resources. It is equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, which maps to 1 physical core and 2 threads. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is supported by a 100 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a highly polarized capability profile. The processor achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 10%, and demonstrates strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core stress-ng performance and large-block memory bandwidth read/write speeds are average. Conversely, the instance shows weak performance in Passmark CPU tests, database operations, and Redis SET operations, while static web serving throughput is poor, landing in the bottom 10%.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without intensive multi-threaded processing demands. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores ensure stable execution, but the weak database and Redis benchmark results suggest it is less suited for high-throughput transactional databases. It is best utilized for memory-optimized general-purpose workloads, single-threaded data processing, lightweight caching, or small-scale LLM text generation.
description: The Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-100s-amd is an x86_64 virtual server from the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with 2 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs (1 physical core, 2 threads) running at 2.0 GHz. It features 16.0 GB of RAM, a 100 GB NVMe SSD, and one complimentary public IPv4 address. Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast: single-core CPU execution is top-tier and single-threaded compression is strong, but multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are average, while database operations, Redis SET throughput, and static web serving are weak to poor. With a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this memory-optimized instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy, single-threaded workloads, lightweight caching, and basic data processing, rather than high-throughput database or web-serving applications.
